newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan fails to agree on China truck engine output.
newsitem.headline: Nissan fails to agree on China truck engine output.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Friday that it had failed to reach an agreement with a Chinese company on producing engines for small trucks in Nanjing.
"We did not reach an agreement as our conditions did not meet their conditions," a company spokesman said.
He could not provide any details on the agreement Nissan had failed to reach with the counter-party, a Nanjing-based vehicle maker.
He added that despite the failure, Nissan would continue to seek to expand its business in China in various fields, including engine production.

The Japanese economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday that Nissan had been negotiating with the Chinese company from late last year with the aim of producing 150,000 2,400 cc engines for small trucks per year.
The total investment envisaged was about 20 billion yen, the paper said.
Nissan abandoned the plan because of a slowdown in vehicle demand in China, the paper said.
Ford Motor Co has also been negotiating with the same Chinese company on a similar engine project, the paper said.
